references.text: Another Pharisee also invited Jesus to eat at his house. In [ref:Luk 7:36|Luke 7:36], we see a similar case where a Pharisee asks Jesus to come and dine with him, showing that some Pharisees were curious about Jesus and wanted to associate with him, even though they were often critical.

Also in [ref:Luk 14:1|Luke 14:1], Jesus is invited to eat at the home of one of the leading Pharisees, where they watched him closely. The Gospel of Luke contains several accounts of Jesus as a guest of Pharisees, and each time confrontations arise concerning God's will.

The immediate continuation in [ref:Luk 11:38-39|Luke 11:38-39] shows that the Pharisee was surprised that Jesus did not wash before the meal, which led to Jesus' judgment on the Pharisees' external purity without inner cleansing.

In [ref:Mark 7:1-5|Mark 7:1-5], the Pharisees and scribes confront Jesus because his disciples eat without washing their hands according to tradition. This is thematically parallel to what happens after Jesus sits down to eat without washing.

In [ref:Matt 15:1-2|Matthew 15:1-2], the Pharisees and scribes criticize Jesus' disciples for not washing their hands before eating, which connects to the Pharisees' focus on external purity laws that also form the background here.

In [ref:Matt 23:25-26|Matthew 23:25-26], Jesus speaks against the Pharisees because they clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and uncontrolled desire. This is thematically parallel to the rebuke that follows the meal invitation in Luke 11.

In [ref:Luk 11:53-54|Luke 11:53-54], we see the result of this meal: the scribes and Pharisees began to press him hard and tried to catch him in something he said. The invitation may have had a hidden agenda.
